summary: The change makes the source generator null-safe for members of closed generic value types defined in referenced assemblies (GetPropertyIdentifierLocation and FirstOrDefault() syntax access), so building no longer crashes with CS8785/AD0001 and a resolver is generated; it also wraps diagnostic reporting in ReportIfLocatedInCompilation to avoid reporting locations outside the compilation being analyzed. The build passes and the three new metadata-reference tests pass. However, ReportIfLocatedInCompilation's condition is inverted (`!ContainsSyntaxTree`), so it drops all diagnostics for types declared in the current compilation and causes 40 newly failing tests (REQ-2283-N1 not met), and tests.fail_without_fix was not run (REQ-2283-N2 unverified). The change should not merge until the filter is corrected.

findings.title: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation filters in the wrong direction
findings.claim: The condition `diagnostic.Location.IsInSource && !this.compilation.ContainsSyntaxTree(diagnostic.Location.SourceTree)` reports a diagnostic only when its source tree is absent from the current compilation—the opposite of the documented intent ('only when its location belongs to the compilation being analyzed'). As a result all analyzer diagnostics for types declared in the current compilation are silenced, which is exactly why 40 previously passing analyzer tests now fail (expected N, actual 0). REQ-2283-N1 is violated and the change must not merge until the condition is corrected.

evidence.quote: this.reportDiagnostic = reportAnalyzerDiagnostic is null ? null : diagnostic => ReportIfLocatedInCompilation(reportAnalyzerDiagnostic, diagnostic);

findings.suggested_fix: Replace `!this.compilation.ContainsSyntaxTree(diagnostic.Location.SourceTree)` with `this.compilation.ContainsSyntaxTree(diagnostic.Location.SourceTree)` so a diagnostic is reported only when its syntax tree belongs to the compilation being analyzed, then re-run the full suite.
